full_name: Securities and Exchange Board of India
access_summary: The 2026-09-04 conclusion that SEBI blocks server-side fetches was WRONG in substance: the only thing that 403s is the directory-style URL https://www.sebi.gov.in/filings/takeovers/ (with trailing slash). Everything that matters is reachable with a plain curl using a browser User-Agent: the homepage (HTTP 200), the static landing page /filings/takeovers.html (200), all detail pages under /filings/takeovers/<mon-yyyy>/<slug>_<id>.html (200), all PDFs under /sebi_data/commondocs/ and /sebi_data/attachdocs/ (200, application/pdf), sitemap.xml (200), sebirss.xml (200) and - the key finding - the underlying listing servlet https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=<section>&ssid=<subsection>&smid=<subsubsection> which returns fully server-rendered HTML including the result table, the record count and the search form (200, ~37 KB). No JavaScript is needed to read any listing or any document; JS is needed only for the paging links and the GO button. WebFetch also worked on the HomeAction.do listing URL and returned the same table. archive.org has copies of the static statistics pages but has NO snapshot of /filings/takeovers, so archive was not needed and would not have helped; every finding below comes from the LIVE site. The earlier "OtherAction.do returned 1 to 0 of 0 records" was a dead-end endpoint - the correct servlet is HomeAction.do.
overall_summary: SEBI is a genuinely usable free source for Indian public-market M&A, and it is much richer than a bare announcement feed. Deal-level coverage comes from three complementary places: (1) Filings > Takeovers, ~2,720 entries back to 2002 (~46-176 per year, 119 in 2025), where each entry is one open offer and accumulates the full statutory document chain as PDFs - Public Announcement, Detailed Public Statement, Draft Letter of Offer, Letter of Offer, pre-offer advertisement, post-offer reports; (2) Statistics > Open Offers, a clean server-rendered HTML table of every open offer with target, acquirers/PACs, PA date, SEBI comment date, opening/closing dates, share count, % of equity, deal value in Rs crore, offer price, object of the offer, post-offer stake and payment mode - back to FY1997-98, but apparently frozen since Feb 2025; and (3) Filings > Processing Status > Takeovers, weekly PDFs that are effectively a live deal pipeline (target, acquirer, merchant banker, PA/DPS/draft-document dates, offer size, last SEBI communication, processing status), plus a matching pipeline for draft schemes of arrangement and for buybacks. Adjacent sections cover buybacks (~1,940 entries), merger/amalgamation schemes via Notice For Meeting on Schemes (354 NCLT scheme notices), Regulation 11 exemption orders and SAST enforcement orders, and SAST informal-guidance/no-action letters. The main gaps: SEBI hosts NO delisting offer documents and NO SAST Regulation 29/31 stake and encumbrance disclosures - those live only on BSE/NSE, which is exactly where scraping is prohibited; scheme observation letters are issued through the exchanges, so SEBI shows only the pipeline status and the shareholder-meeting notices; there is no API, no JSON endpoint, no XBRL and no Excel export; and server-side paging beyond the first 25 rows requires a JS-driven POST. Coverage is limited to listed-company control events - no private-deal or unlisted M&A. For a free India source it is the best of the three (SEBI / BSE / NSE) because it is the only one whose terms do not prohibit automated access.
company_info_verdict: Yes - SEBI goes well beyond announcements. A Letter of Offer is a 70-90 page prospectus-grade document on the parties: it carries a dedicated 'Background of the Acquirers and the PACs' section with each acquirer's and PAC's incorporation history, registered office, ownership/shareholding pattern, board and promoters, and three years of audited financials (revenue, PAT, net worth, EPS) converted to INR; a 'Details of the Seller' section; and a 'Background of the Target Company' section with the target's CIN, incorporation and name-change history, listing/ISIN/scrip code, line of business, authorised and paid-up capital, three years of audited P&L and balance sheet, and a pre-/post-offer shareholding table by category. The Public Announcement and DPS add the transaction mechanics - SPA date and parties, price per share, aggregate consideration, % acquired, offer price and its computation, conditions precedent such as CCI and lender approvals. So SEBI supplies acquirer and target descriptions, financials and shareholding, not just deal headlines. What it does not supply is a per-company profile page or any entity master - the company information is buried inside per-deal PDFs and must be parsed out of them.
blockers: Directory-style URL https://www.sebi.gov.in/filings/takeovers/ (trailing slash) returns HTTP 403; use /filings/takeovers.html or the HomeAction.do servlet instead. This single 403 is what caused the earlier false 'SEBI blocks scraping' conclusion.

Server-side paging is not reachable by GET: adding nextValue / pageNo / page / startValue / currentPage / pno to HomeAction.do always returns page 1 (rows 1-25). The paging links call a JS function that POSTs the form.

The POST search cannot be replayed with curl alone: it needs the jsessionid-rewritten action URL plus an org.apache.struts.taglib.html.TOKEN whose value is rendered as literal '...' in the HTML and is filled in by JavaScript held under /js, which robots.txt disallows. All POST attempts returned HTTP 302 to the session-expiry page.

WORKAROUND that removes the paging blocker: GET filters DO work - doListing=yes accepts &search=<entity name>, &fromDate=DD-MM-YYYY&toDate=DD-MM-YYYY and &deptId=. Narrowing to a month or a week keeps every result set under 25 rows, so a full historical crawl is possible by date-slicing without ever POSTing.
No API, no JSON/XHR endpoint, no XBRL, no CSV/Excel download button anywhere in the M&A sections. All deal data is HTML tables or PDF.

The 'Daily Status: Offer Documents where Final Observation Issued / Withdrawn / Returned' link goes to an embedded Zoho Sheet on sheet.publicmgovcloud.in that renders only in JavaScript and shows a Zoho sign-up wall to a server-side fetch - not machine-readable.

Delisting (voluntary delisting / going private) offer documents are NOT hosted by SEBI at all - there is no Delisting sub-section under Filings and none under Processing Status. Only the Delisting Regulations and delisting FAQs are on SEBI.

SAST Regulation 29 / 31 disclosures (5%+ stake changes, encumbrances) are NOT on SEBI - only the blank formats are. The filled disclosures go to the stock exchanges, i.e. BSE/NSE, whose terms prohibit scraping.

The structured Statistics > Open Offers table appears frozen: the newest page is 'April 1, 2024 - Feb 28, 2025' and probes for mar2025/apr2025/.../aug2026 all return HTTP 404. Recent deals must be taken from the Takeovers filings and the weekly Processing Status PDFs instead.

Copyright Policy on the Website Policy page requires permission by e-mail before reproducing material ('may be reproduced free of charge after taking proper permission by sending a mail to us') - free, but a redistribution/publication constraint to note. The Terms of Use themselves are silent on automated access or scraping.
Most Processing Status and Final Observations PDFs are bilingual Hindi/English with merged cells; pdftotext -layout keeps them readable but rows misalign, so table extraction needs care.
Coverage is listed-company control events only. No unlisted/private M&A, no deal rationale, no advisor league-table data beyond the merchant banker name.

sections.name: Filings > Takeovers (Letter of Offer) - open offer document chain
sections.what_it_is: The core repository of SEBI (SAST) Regulations open offers. One list entry per open offer / target company; the entry's detail page accumulates every statutory document of that offer as a PDF, dated. The parent section (smid=0) also has 'Other Documents' and 'Formats'; the human-facing landing page is https://www.sebi.gov.in/filings/takeovers.html and the JS-free listing is the HomeAction.do URL above.
sections.data_form: HTML table (2 columns) linking to per-deal HTML pages, each of which is a dated list of PDF links
sections.example_document_contents: Two real documents opened. (a) Public Announcement for Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri Limited (11 pages, https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/commondocs/sep-2026/Tribhovandas%20Bhimji%20Zaveri%20Limited%20-%20PA_p.pdf): names the target (TBZ Ltd, registered office 241/43 Zaveri Bazar Mumbai), the acquirer (GRT Jewellers (India) Private Limited), the six named sellers (Shrikant Gopaldas Zaveri, Bindu/Binaisha/Raashi Zaveri, TBZ Private Limited, TBZ Jewellers (Mumbai) Private Limited), the manager to the offer (Axis Capital Limited), the SPA dated 31 August 2026 for 4,94,59,775 shares = 74.12% of voting capital at INR 209.00 per share for up to INR 10,337,092,975, the resulting mandatory open offer for 1,72,70,845 shares = 25.88% at INR 249.61 per share = up to INR 4,31,09,75,621, offer type (triggered, not competing, not conditional), conditions precedent (CCI approval, named lenders' approval), a tabular 'Details of Underlying Transaction', and the acquirer/target/seller identification blocks. (b) Letter of Offer for Novartis India Limited (https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/commondocs/jun-2026/Novartis%20India%20Limited%20-%20LOF_p.pdf, ~6,300 text lines) with sections: I Key Definitions, II Disclaimer, III Details of the Open Offer (SPA salient features, underlying transaction table, FEMA/FDI limits, proposed renaming of the target), IV Background of the Acquirers and the PACs (per acquirer and per PAC: incorporation, registered office, shareholding pattern, directors, and three years of audited financials - revenue, PAT, net worth, EPS, converted from USD to INR), V Details of Novartis AG (Seller), VI Background of the Target Company (CIN L24200MH1947PLC006104, incorporation 13 Dec 1947 as CIBA Pharma Private Limited plus full name-change history, BSE scrip code 500672, ISIN INE234A01025, business = manufacture/wholesale trading of pharmaceutical goods, authorised capital INR 32,00,00,000, paid-up INR 12,34,53,985 / 2,46,90,797 shares, three-year P&L and balance sheet with EPS 37.74 / 40.87 / 34.50, and a pre-/post-offer shareholding table by category showing promoter group 1,74,50,680 = 70.68% moving to the acquirers at 72.78% post-offer), VII Offer Price and Financial Arrangements (justification of offer price), VIII Terms and Conditions incl. statutory approvals, IX Procedure for Acceptance, X Tax, XI Documents for Inspection, plus a Schedule of Major Activities giving every offer milestone date. This is the single richest company-level artefact on the site.
sections.filters: GET-accessible and confirmed working: &search=<title / keyword / entity name> (e.g. search=Reliance -> 4 records, search=Novartis -> 2 records), &fromDate=DD-MM-YYYY&toDate=DD-MM-YYYY, &deptId= (-1 all / 1 Corporation Finance Department / 9 Investment Management Department), &smid= (15 Letter of Offer, 50 Formats as per SEBI (SAST) Regulations 2011, 49 Other Documents, 0 or -1 all). Cross-filings search also works with sid=3&ssid=-1&smid=-1&search=Novartis (8 records). Paging is NOT GET-accessible - date-slice instead.
sections.history_from: Effectively 2002. Date probes: 1997-1998 = 0 records, 2000-2001 = 1 record, 2002 = 146, 2003 = 367, 2004 = 246. So usable history starts 2002-2003.
sections.volume_estimate: 2,721-2,723 records in the parent Takeovers section; 2,125 under 'Letter of Offer'; 592 under 'Other Documents'; 1 under 'Formats'. Per year: 2002 = 146, 2003 = 367, 2004 = 246, 2005 = 176, 2015 = 76, 2020 = 46, 2025 = 119, 2026 to 08-Sep = 77. Roughly 50-120 open offers a year recently. Note one list entry can carry 5+ PDFs.
sections.formats: Listing = server-rendered HTML. Detail page = HTML. Documents = PDF (text-layer PDFs, pdftotext-extractable; typically 0.3-1.4 MB, 10-90 pages). No XBRL, no Excel.
sections.company_info: Very high. Acquirer/PAC identity, incorporation, ownership, directors and 3 years of audited financials; seller identity; target CIN, ISIN, scrip code, incorporation and naming history, business description, share capital, 3 years of audited P&L and balance sheet with EPS; pre- and post-offer shareholding pattern by category. Also the merchant banker / manager to the offer and the registrar.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the HomeAction.do listing (37,536 bytes), HTTP 200 on /filings/takeovers.html, HTTP 200 on every detail page, HTTP 200 application/pdf on the documents; HTTP 403 only on the trailing-slash /filings/takeovers/. WebFetch ok - returned the same headers, record count '1 to 25 of 2723 records' and first rows. JS needed: no for reading, yes for paging/GO button. archive.org: no snapshot of /filings/takeovers (wayback availability API returned empty), and not needed.
sections.notes: Detail-page URL pattern /filings/takeovers/<mon-yyyy>/<slug>_<numericId>.html and document pattern /sebi_data/commondocs/<mon-yyyy>/<name>_p.pdf are both stable and directly crawlable. The document label ('Public Announcement', 'Detailed Public Statement', 'Draft Letter of Offer', 'Letter of Offer', 'Pre-offer advertisement') is shown next to each PDF with its own date, so the offer timeline can be reconstructed from the detail page alone without opening the PDFs.

sections.name: Statistics > Open Offers - structured open-offer deal table
sections.what_it_is: The most machine-friendly M&A dataset on the site: an index of ~140 static HTML pages, each a cumulative table of every open offer made under the SAST Regulations for a financial year up to a stated month. Exactly one row per deal with quantitative fields.
column_headers: In terms of Value ( Rs cr )
Post offer stake of Acquirer in % (assuming full response in the offer)
example_row: ZEST HOLDING INVESTMENTS LIMITED, ZEST INVESTMENTS LIMITED, SAMARA CAPITAL PARTNERS FUND III LIMITED, INFINITY HOLDINGS, INFINITY HOLDINGS SIDECAR 1
sections.example_document_contents: Not a document but the table itself, headed 'DETAILS OF OPEN OFFERS MADE UNDER SEBI (SUBSTANTIAL ACQUISITION OF SHARES AND TAKEOVERS) REGULATIONS, 2011 / During the period from 01 April 2024 - 28 February 2025 / Updation on Monthly basis'. The 'Object of the offer' field is a useful categorical: observed values include 'Change in control', 'Consolidation of holdings' and (in the 1997-regime pages) 'SUBSTANTIAL ACQUISITION'. The earliest pages use a different, in some ways richer header set - apr1997.html reads 'S.No | TARGET COMPANY | ACQUIRER | OFFER OPENING DATE | OFFER CLOSING DATE | OFFER SIZE (No. of shares / % of equity) | OFFER PRICE | OBJECT OF THE OFFER | TARGETED POST OFFER STAKE OF ACQ (%AGE of equity capital) | MERCHANT BANKER | REGISTRAR', i.e. it names the merchant banker and registrar, which the modern layout dropped.
sections.filters: None - no search box, no query parameters. Selection is by choosing one of the ~140 period pages from the index. Each page is cumulative for its financial year, so one page per FY is enough.
sections.history_from: FY1997-98 (https://www.sebi.gov.in/statistics/open-offers/apr1997.html, 'Offers Opened During 01 April 1997 - 31 March 1998'), continuous through FY2024-25.
sections.volume_estimate: ~140 period pages. Deal rows: ~40 offers in FY1997-98 (45 table rows), ~60 offers in Apr 2024 - Feb 2025 (67 table rows). Cumulatively on the order of 2,000-3,000 open-offer rows across 28 years.
sections.formats: Static HTML only. No Excel/CSV export.
sections.company_info: Deal-level only: target name, acquirer/PAC names (often several, comma-separated), and in pre-2011 pages the merchant banker and registrar. No financials, no business descriptions, no shareholding detail - for those, join the target name to the Takeovers filings section above.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the index (24,826 bytes) and on both feb2025.html (43,490 bytes) and apr1997.html (32,167 bytes). WebFetch not needed. JS needed: no. archive.org: yes, snapshot 2026-07-07 confirmed available for the index page.
sections.notes: APPARENTLY DISCONTINUED. The newest page is feb2025.html (April 1, 2024 - Feb 28, 2025); direct probes of mar2025, apr2025, jun2025, sep2025, dec2025, feb2026, mar2026, jun2026 and aug2026 all returned HTTP 404, and the index lists nothing newer. Treat this as a high-quality historical backfile through Feb 2025 and use the Processing Status PDFs plus the Takeovers filings for anything after that. The two-level header (a group row 'Offer Schedule' / 'Offer Size' / 'Offer features' above the leaf row) means an HTML table parser must flatten two header rows.

sections.name: Filings > Processing Status > Takeovers - weekly open-offer pipeline
sections.what_it_is: A weekly-updated pair of PDF reports on the status of draft offer documents under the SAST Regulations: 'Pending Offer documents as on <date>' (deals still in SEBI review) and 'Final Observations Issued for The Offer Documents issued during the Financial Year <FY>' (deals cleared). This is effectively SEBI's live M&A pipeline, including deals whose LOF is not yet public.
sections.data_form: PDF list (an HTML hub page whose links are dated PDF tables)
example_row: Shareholders' approval has been received but in-principle approval of Exchanges for Delisting is pending.
sections.example_document_contents: 'PROCESSING STATUS OF DRAFT OFFER DOCUMENTS AS ON SEPTEMBER 4, 2026' (bilingual Hindi/English, 464 KB): a table of open offers under SEBI review with, per row, target company, acquirer, merchant banker, PA date, DPS date, date the draft offer document was received, offer size in Rs crore, the last communication issued or received, and a free-text processing status. Real rows seen: Federal Mogul Goetze India Limited / Pegasus Holdings III, LLC and Pegasus Parent, L.P. / BofA Securities India Limited / PA 23-Feb-22 / DPS 29-Nov-22 / DOD 01-Dec-22 / Rs 411.00 cr / 'Pending in Supreme Court... The matter is sub-judice'; SRI SARVARAYA SUGARS LIMITED / DREAM ACHIEVER CONSULTANCY SERVICES PRIVATE LIMITED / Corpwis Advisors Private Limited / Rs 31.06 cr / 'Enforcement Directorate has frozen the assets of the Acquirer... sub-judice'; Krishna Capital and Securities Limited / Ashu Bishnoi and Yagnik Tank / Grow House Wealth Management / PA 26-Mar-26 / Rs 3.61 cr / 'Clarification sought on August 19, 2026 - Reply awaited'. The companion 'FINAL OBSERVATIONS ISSUED FOR DRAFT OFFER DOCUMENTS DURING THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2025-26 AS ON SEPTEMBER 4, 2026' (389 KB) has columns Sl.No / Target Company / Acquirer / Merchant Banker / PA Date / DPS Date / DOD received on / Offer Size (Rupees in crores) / Date of Final Comments, with rows such as 'Stylam Industries Limited / AICA KOGYO COMPANY, LIMITED / ICICI Securities Limited / 13/02/2026 / 23/02/2026 / 02/03/2026 / 09/04/2026' and 'AAA TECNOLOGIES LIMITED / Jyotirgamya Advisory Private Limited, Mr. Ashok Kumar Chordia / Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited'.
sections.filters: The hub page itself is a plain link list, no filters. The parent Processing Status listing (https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=3&ssid=14&smid=0, 8 records) supports the same &search= / &fromDate= / &toDate= GET filters, with sub-sub-sections smid=8 Issues, 9 Takeovers, 62 Scheme of Arrangement, 116 Buybacks.
sections.history_from: One PDF per financial year on the hub page, from 'Observations issued till March 2016' (posted Oct 2017) through FY2026-27, i.e. a continuous FY series from 2016-17 onward plus a pre-2016 cumulative file.
sections.volume_estimate: 12 PDFs currently linked on the hub page (one 'pending' snapshot plus one 'final observations' file per FY). Refreshed weekly - the file states 'Updated on weekly basis. Next update shall be for the week ending September 11, 2026'. Each FY file lists roughly 60-120 offers; the pending file typically a few dozen.
sections.formats: PDF only (text-layer, pdftotext -layout works). Bilingual Hindi/English headers. No HTML or Excel version.
sections.company_info: Party names only (target, acquirer, merchant banker) plus deal size and regulatory status - no financials or descriptions. Its unique value is the MERCHANT BANKER field and the free-text status, which reveal deal problems (litigation at SAT/Supreme Court, ED asset freezes, revoked exchange approvals, pending delisting in-principle approval) that appear nowhere else.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the hub page (10,498 bytes) and HTTP 200 application/pdf on both weekly PDFs (464,246 and 388,935 bytes). WebFetch not attempted (curl sufficed). JS needed: no. archive.org: not needed.
sections.notes: The PDF filenames change every week (e.g. 'pending -04.09_p.pdf', 'Final-04.09_p.pdf') so a crawler must re-read the hub page each week rather than guessing URLs. Merged cells mean rows can misalign in text extraction - the Federal Mogul / BLB / G D Trading rows above are visibly interleaved in the raw text output, so treat cell-level extraction as needing validation.

sections.name: Filings > Processing Status > Scheme of Arrangement - draft merger scheme pipeline
sections.what_it_is: Weekly status report on draft schemes of arrangement (mergers, amalgamations, demergers of listed companies) filed with the stock exchanges and routed to SEBI for observations. Delivered as a PDF embedded in an iframe on the hub page.
sections.data_form: PDF list (single PDF embedded via iframe)
column_headers: Date of filing of Scheme with Exchange(s)
sections.example_document_contents: 'PROCESSING STATUS OF DRAFT SCHEMES AS ON SEPTEMBER 4, 2026' (289 KB). Grouped by status category, the first being 'I. Comments/NOC/Complaints report awaited from stock exchange(s)'. Rows are the listed applicant company, one or more dates of filing with the exchange(s), the last communication, and the processing status. Real applicants listed: Mangalam Worldwide Limited, Vikas EcoTech Limited, Vadilal Industries Limited, Diligent Media Corporation Ltd, Hubtown Ltd, Modern Insulators Limited, EMA India Ltd, Panther Industrial Products Ltd, National Fittings Ltd. It gives no counterparty, no consideration and no scheme terms - only the applicant and where the file sits in the process.
sections.filters: None on the document. The parent listing (sid=3&ssid=14&smid=62) has only 2 records and supports the standard &search= / &fromDate= / &toDate= GET filters.
sections.history_from: Only the current snapshot is published; the linked PDF is regenerated in place, so no back series is retained on this page. Older snapshots would have to come from archive.org.
sections.volume_estimate: 2 records in the listing; one live PDF, refreshed weekly, listing a few dozen pending draft schemes at a time.
sections.formats: PDF (embedded in an iframe on the HTML page).
sections.company_info: Minimal - applicant company name only. No counterparty, no financials, no swap ratio.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the hub page; the PDF URL must be scraped out of the iframe src (naive href extraction picks up the truncated attribute and fails with curl exit/HTTP 000) - once the clean URL /sebi_data/attachdocs/sep-2026/1788519353259.pdf is used, curl returns HTTP 200 application/pdf (289,436 bytes). WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: no (the iframe src is in the served HTML). archive.org: not tested.
sections.notes: Important scope point for the team: SEBI does NOT publish the scheme observation letters or the draft scheme documents themselves - those are issued to and hosted by BSE/NSE. SEBI shows only the pipeline status here and the NCLT shareholder-meeting notices in the separate section below. The PDF path uses an opaque timestamp filename that changes on each refresh, so it must be re-scraped from the iframe each time.

sections.name: Filings > Buybacks
sections.what_it_is: Buyback offer documents, split into 'Tender Offers' (smid=17) and 'Open Market Through Stock Exchanges' (smid=18). Same listing-plus-detail-page-plus-PDF structure as Takeovers. Relevant to M&A as a capital-return and promoter-stake-consolidation signal.
sections.data_form: HTML table (2 columns) linking to per-company pages of dated PDFs
sections.example_document_contents: The Tips Music Limited detail page (breadcrumb 'Filings > Buybacks > Open Market Through Stock Exchanges', dated Sep 04, 2026) carries one dated PDF: '04-09-2026 | Public Announcement'. A buyback Public Announcement or Letter of Offer states the company, the buyback route (tender / open market), maximum shares and maximum price, the buyback size in Rs crore and as a % of paid-up capital and free reserves, promoter participation, the record date and the pre-/post-buyback shareholding pattern. Note: the tender-offer letter of offer includes the company's own audited financials, but a buyback has no acquirer, so there is no counterparty background section as in a takeover LOF.
sections.filters: Same GET-accessible filters as Takeovers: &search=, &fromDate=/&toDate=, &deptId=, and &smid= (17 Tender Offers, 18 Open Market Through Stock Exchanges).
sections.formats: HTML listing and detail pages; PDF documents. No Excel.
sections.company_info: Moderate. Issuer identity and capital structure, buyback economics, promoter stake before and after; tender-offer letters of offer add the issuer's audited financials. No counterparty information (there is none).
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the listing (37,355 bytes) and HTTP 200 on the detail page. WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: no. archive.org: not needed.
sections.notes: A matching pipeline report exists at Filings > Processing Status > Buybacks (https://www.sebi.gov.in/filings/processing-status/may-2023/processing-status-buy-back_47253.html) with FY PDFs 'Final Observations Issued...' for FY2020-21 through FY2023-24 plus 'Pending Offer documents as on May 12, 2023' - but that hub page is dated May 12, 2023 and has not been refreshed since, so the buyback pipeline series appears stale (unlike the takeover one, which is weekly). Documented example: https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/commondocs/may-2023/Buyback%2012.05.2023-Pending_p.pdf

sections.name: Reports & Statistics > Notice For Meeting on Schemes - merger / amalgamation scheme documents
sections.what_it_is: NCLT-directed notices convening shareholder and creditor meetings to approve schemes of amalgamation, merger, demerger and arrangement of listed companies, plus the accompanying newspaper advertisements. This is SEBI's only deal-document coverage of NCLT-route M&A (as opposed to open offers).
sections.data_form: HTML table (2 columns) linking to detail pages or directly to PDFs
example_row: Notice convening the Meeting of the Equity Shareholders of Ambuja Cements Limited (“Transferee Company” or “Company”) pursuant to the Order passed by the Hon’ble National Company Law Tribunal, Ahmedabad Bench (“Hon’ble Tribunal”) in respect of Scheme of Amalgamation of Orient Cement Limited with Ambuja Cements Limited (“Scheme”)
sections.example_document_contents: Not opened in full, but the row titles themselves already carry the deal: they name the transferor company, the transferee company, the NCLT bench and the scheme type - e.g. four consecutive Aug 2026 entries covering the 'Scheme of Amalgamation of Orient Cement Limited with Ambuja Cements Limited', separately for each company's shareholder meeting plus the newspaper advertisements. A further real row is 'NOTICE OF MEETING OF THE UNSECURED CREDITORS OF ACCEL LIMITED CONVENED PURSUANT TO THE ORDER DATED 27th JUNE 2025 OF THE HON'BLE NATIONAL COMPANY LAW TRIBUNAL, CHENNAI BENCH'. An NCLT scheme notice of this kind conventionally attaches the scheme of arrangement itself, the share exchange ratio, the valuation report and fairness opinion, the audit committee report and the pre-/post-scheme capital structure - but that content was INFERRED from the document type, not verified by opening one.
sections.filters: Standard GET-accessible filters confirmed: &search=amalgamation returns 73 records; &fromDate=/&toDate= works (2020 = 28, 2024 = 31, 2025 = 18, 2026 = 5).
sections.history_from: Not before 2020 in the date probes tested: 2010 = 0 records, 2015 = 0 records, 2020 = 28 records. Total 354 records suggests the bulk sits in 2020-2026.
sections.volume_estimate: 354 records total; roughly 18-31 per year in 2020-2025, and 5 recorded for 2026 to date. Several records per deal (one per company, plus the advertisement).
sections.formats: HTML detail pages and PDF attachments.
sections.company_info: Party names and roles (transferor / transferee) are explicit in the titles. Deeper information - swap ratio, valuation, financials - is expected inside the attached notices but was NOT verified here.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the listing (51,712 bytes); the &search= and date-range filters returned working record counts. Individual notice documents were not opened. WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: no. archive.org: not tested.
sections.notes: The team should open two or three of these notices before relying on them, since the scheme terms (share exchange ratio, valuation) are the valuable part and were not verified. Also note the listing lives under /reports-and-statistics/ not /filings/, and is reached via sid=4 not sid=3.

sections.name: Enforcement > Orders - Regulation 11 exemption orders and SAST enforcement orders
sections.what_it_is: All SEBI orders, sub-divided by type (smid=1 Orders of SAT, 2 Orders of Chairman/Members, 3 Settlement Orders, 6 Orders of AO, 54 Orders on Insider Trading, 7 Orders of Courts, 77 Orders of Special Courts, 4 Orders of AA under RTI, 5 Corporatisation/Demutualisation). Includes the Regulation 11 open-offer exemption orders the team asked about, and orders penalising SAST violations.
sections.data_form: HTML table (2 columns) linking to detail pages with the order PDF
example_row: Order for exemption under regulation 11 of Takeover Regulations, 2011 in the matter of Batliboi Limited
sections.example_document_contents: Order PDFs were not opened. Based on the titles, Regulation 11 orders decide applications to be exempted from the mandatory open offer - e.g. 'Order in respect of application filed by Mrugesh Jaykrishna Family Trust - 2 under regulation 11 of Takeover Regulations, 2011 for acquisition of shares in AksharChem (India) Limited'. Such orders conventionally recite the applicant, the target, the proposed acquisition and shareholding before and after, the reason for the exemption request (intra-promoter/family transfer, restructuring, bank recapitalisation) and SEBI's reasoning - i.e. they disclose intra-group and promoter-family transfers that never trigger a public open offer and therefore appear in no other section. That content is INFERRED from the titles and order type, not verified by opening a document.
sections.filters: Standard GET-accessible filters confirmed working: smid=2&search=takeover -> 66 records; smid=6&search=takeover -> 1; smid=3&search=takeover -> 2; smid=0&search=exemption -> 219 records. &fromDate=/&toDate= also apply.
sections.history_from: Not systematically probed. Orders returned by the searches above go back to at least 2016; the section as a whole (30,883 records) plainly reaches back much further.
sections.volume_estimate: 30,883 records across all order types - overwhelmingly not M&A. M&A-relevant slice is small: 66 hits for 'takeover' in Orders of Chairman/Members, 219 for 'exemption' across all orders, 1-2 in AO and Settlement orders.
sections.formats: HTML detail pages with PDF orders.
sections.company_info: Party names, the target, and (inside the order) the shareholding before and after the proposed acquisition. No financials. Unique value: intra-promoter and exempted transfers that produce no open offer.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the listing and on every filtered search variant tried; record counts returned as expected. Individual order PDFs not opened. WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: no. archive.org: not tested.
sections.notes: Very low signal-to-noise - 30,883 records of which only a few hundred are M&A. Only worth ingesting via targeted &search= queries ('regulation 11', 'takeover', 'exemption', 'Substantial Acquisition'), not by bulk crawl.

sections.name: Enforcement > Informal Guidance - SAST interpretive letters and no-action letters
sections.what_it_is: Requests for informal guidance (interpretive letters and 'no action' letters) and SEBI's replies. A meaningful minority concern the SAST Regulations - i.e. named companies asking in advance whether a contemplated transaction triggers an open offer.
sections.data_form: HTML table (2 columns) linking to detail pages with the request and reply
example_row: Request for Informal Guidance by way of a 'No action' letter under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Informal Guidance) Scheme, 2025 received from Saint Gobain Sekurit Automotive Private Limited in relation to the provisions of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
sections.example_document_contents: Documents not opened. The titles alone identify the requester and the regulation at issue - e.g. Saint Gobain Sekurit Automotive Private Limited on the SAST Regulations, CHL Ltd on the Takeover Regulations, Empire Industries Limited and Pritish Nandy Communications Limited on SAST. An informal-guidance letter conventionally sets out the applicant's proposed transaction in detail and SEBI's view on whether an open offer is triggered - a forward-looking signal of intended restructurings. INFERRED from document type, not verified.
sections.filters: GET-accessible filters confirmed: &search=takeover -> 43 records; &search=Takeovers also returns SAST-specific rows; &fromDate=/&toDate= works (2003 = 3, 2005 = 16, 2010 = 18).
sections.volume_estimate: 481 records total, of which 43 match 'takeover'. Roughly 15-20 requests per year overall, only a handful SAST-related.
sections.formats: HTML detail pages with PDF letters.
sections.company_info: Requester name and the transaction it is contemplating. No financials. Value is early-warning, not company profiling.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the listing (54,298 bytes) and on the filtered searches. Individual letters not opened. WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: no. archive.org: not tested.
sections.notes: Small but high-quality: these are named companies telling SEBI in advance about a planned control transaction. Worth a monthly &search=Takeovers poll rather than a bulk crawl.

sections.name: Topic listing 'Takeover' (cross-section aggregation, cid=6)
sections.what_it_is: A subject-tag view that pulls together everything on the site tagged 'Takeover' - takeover filings plus the related circulars, regulations, FAQs and orders - in one list. Useful as a single crawl seed spanning multiple sections.
sections.example_document_contents: Rows link straight into the same per-deal takeover pages described in the Takeovers section, so document contents are identical (PA / DPS / DLOF / LOF PDFs).
sections.filters: &search= appears to be accepted on the URL but returned no record-count line in the two probes tried (cid=6&search=delisting, cid=1&search=delisting), so treat cid-level search as unverified. Date filters not tested here.
sections.history_from: Not established - the default sort is not strictly reverse-chronological (the first page starts at Jul 2019), so the listing order is unreliable.
sections.formats: HTML listing; targets are the usual HTML pages and PDFs.
sections.company_info: Same as the underlying sections it aggregates.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 (42,640 bytes), record count '1 to 25 of 1856 records' read directly. WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: no. archive.org: not tested.
sections.notes: The odd sort order and the unverified search make this less useful than sid=3&ssid=20 for systematic collection. There are 34 such topic ids on the homepage; cid=6 is 'Takeover', cid=1 'Issues And Listing', cid=65 'Listing Regulations'.

sections.name: Site-wide RSS feed
sections.what_it_is: A standard RSS 2.0 feed of the 30 most recent SEBI publications across all sections - circulars, orders, recovery proceedings, filings. The only push-style interface on the site.
example_row: Relaxation in timeline with respect to Accredited Investor mandate for Angel Funds
Relaxation in timeline with respect to Accredited Investor mandate for Angel Funds
sections.example_document_contents: The feed carries only title, description (a duplicate of the title), link and pubDate - no document body. Channel metadata: title 'SEBI RSS Feed', ttl 60, lastBuildDate '08 Sep 2026 08:00:02', so it is rebuilt daily around 08:00 IST.
sections.filters: None - no per-section feeds were found (rss.xml, /feed and /sebiweb/rss/rss.jsp all returned HTTP 404).
sections.history_from: No history - a rolling window of the latest 30 items only.
sections.volume_estimate: 30 items per snapshot. In the snapshot read, the items were circulars, SAT appeals and recovery-proceeding orders - not a single takeover filing - so takeover coverage in the feed is incidental at best.
sections.company_info: None beyond whatever is in the title.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200, content-type text/xml, 14,744 bytes, 30 <item> elements. WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: no. archive.org: not needed.
sections.notes: Too coarse to be the primary monitor for M&A - a 30-item all-sections window will miss takeover filings on busy days. Better to poll sid=3&ssid=20 with a rolling date filter. The feed is still worth having as a cheap change-detection signal. There is also a full sitemap at https://www.sebi.gov.in/sitemap.xml (HTTP 200, 63,596 bytes, 364 <loc> entries) but it is a curated selection, not a complete index, and contains only a handful of filings URLs.

sections.name: Daily Status of Offer Documents (external Zoho Sheet) - NOT MACHINE-READABLE
sections.what_it_is: Linked from Filings > Processing Status as 'Daily Status: Offer Documents where Final Observation Issued / Withdrawn / Returned' (dated Jun 19, 2026). It is a published spreadsheet hosted off-site on a government Zoho Sheet instance - potentially the most granular and most frequent view of the offer-document pipeline.
sections.example_document_contents: Could not be read. A server-side fetch returns the Zoho Sheet application shell - menus ('Version', 'Function', 'View Settings', 'Pivot', 'Conditional Formatting'), a 'Save to My Account' / 'Create Your Account' sign-up wall and a captcha placeholder - and no cell data. The grid is populated by JavaScript. No column headers or rows are reported here because none were observed.
sections.filters: Unknown - the sheet UI would offer its own filtering, but it was not reachable.
sections.formats: Zoho Sheet web application (JS-rendered). A published-sheet export endpoint may exist but was not found or tested.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 but content is the Zoho application shell with a sign-up wall, not data. WebFetch not attempted. JS needed: YES - this is the one genuinely JS-blocked M&A source found. archive.org: not tested.
sections.notes: Recorded deliberately as a negative result. It is off-site (sheet.publicmgovcloud.in, not sebi.gov.in), so SEBI's terms would not govern it and Zoho's would. If the team ever needs daily rather than weekly pipeline granularity, this is the target - it would need a headless browser, or a request to SEBI for the underlying data. The weekly PDFs cover the same ground and are directly fetchable.

sections.name: Delisting (voluntary delisting / going private) - NOT PUBLISHED BY SEBI
sections.what_it_is: Checked because voluntary delisting is a going-private event the team wants. SEBI hosts no delisting offer documents. The Filings sub-section dropdown contains exactly: Processing Status, Public Issues, Rights Issues, Debt Offer Document, Takeovers, Mutual Funds, Buybacks, InvIT Public/Private/Rights Issues, REIT Issues, SM REIT Issues, Municipal Debt Securities Privately/Public Issues - no Delisting. The Processing Status sub-sections are Issues, Takeovers, Scheme of Arrangement, Buybacks, Regulatory Sandbox - no Delisting. /filings/delisting returns HTTP 404 and the site sitemap.xml contains zero URLs matching 'delist'.
sections.example_document_contents: All that exists on SEBI is the rulebook and guidance, not deal documents: the SEBI (Delisting of Equity Shares) Regulations, 2021 (last amended 25 September 2024) and a delisting FAQ PDF. Delisting public announcements, detailed public statements, letters of offer, reverse-book-building price discovery and post-delisting reports are filed with and published by BSE and NSE. Delisting does surface indirectly in the takeover pipeline - the Processing Status Takeovers PDF row for Nilachal Refractories Limited reads 'in-principle approval of Exchanges for Delisting is pending' - but that is a status note, not a document.
sections.volume_estimate: Zero delisting deal documents on SEBI.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 404 on /filings/delisting; sitemap.xml grep for 'delist' = 0 matches; the Filings and Processing Status sub-section dropdowns were read directly out of the served HTML and contain no Delisting entry. JS needed: no. archive.org: not applicable.
sections.notes: This is a hard gap for the India plan: going-private data sits on BSE/NSE, which prohibit scraping. Options are manual collection, a licensed feed, or accepting the gap. Delisting-linked open offers (Regulation 5A of the SAST Regulations, where the acquirer declares an intention to delist) ARE on SEBI in the Takeovers section, so acquirer-driven delistings are partially covered; company-initiated voluntary delistings are not.

sections.name: SAST Regulation 29 / 31 disclosures (5%+ stake changes, encumbrances) - NOT PUBLISHED BY SEBI
sections.what_it_is: Checked because these disclosures are the earliest signal of stake-building. SEBI publishes only the BLANK FORMS, in Filings > Takeovers > 'Formats as per SEBI (SAST) Regulations 2011' - a single record from Nov 2011. The filled disclosures by acquirers, promoters and pledgors are filed with the target company and the stock exchanges, and are published on BSE and NSE (e.g. NSE's 'Corporate Filings - Regulation 29' page).
sections.example_document_contents: The single SEBI record is 'Formats For Reports/Disclosures as per SEBI (SAST) Regulations 2011' (Nov 2011) - template forms only, containing no company data. Confirmation that the live disclosures sit on the exchanges also comes from inside a SEBI document: the Novartis India Letter of Offer states the target's pre-offer shareholding pattern is 'as on 31 March 2026 as disclosed by the Target Company on the website of the Stock Exchange'.
sections.volume_estimate: 1 record on SEBI. The real disclosure volume - thousands per year - is entirely on BSE/NSE.
sections.access_test: curl HTTP 200 on the Formats listing, which reports '1 to 1 of 1 records'. Cross-checked with one WebSearch restricted to sebi.gov.in / nseindia.com / bseindia.com, which surfaced NSE's Regulation 29 corporate-filings page and the SEBI SAST formats page. JS needed: no. archive.org: not applicable.
sections.confidence: CONFIRMED (absent from SEBI); exchange location PARTLY CONFIRMED via search result and the LOF's own wording
sections.notes: Second hard gap. Stake-building intelligence (Reg 29 5%+ disclosures, Reg 31 encumbrances) requires BSE/NSE, where scraping is prohibited. On SEBI the earliest a deal becomes visible is the Public Announcement - i.e. once the SPA is already signed - or, slightly earlier and only for deals under review, the weekly Processing Status pending list.
